content:
Laredo keeps drawing the top of the Texas ticket. Democratic U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico is scheduled to bring his “Clear Eyes, Full Hearts” tour to Laredo on Sunday, Oct. 25, and Gov. Greg Abbott is also planning a campaign stop in the Gateway City, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Talarico’s tour, announced Oct. 16, spans 20 Texas cities and wraps Nov. 2 in Austin, according to the El Paso Times. The Laredo stop on Oct. 25 is followed by Weslaco the same day and El Paso on Oct. 26 — his fourth visit to the borderlands since announcing his Senate campaign in September 2025. Talarico will face Republican Ken Paxton on Nov. 3 for a chance to represent Texas in the U.S. Senate. Paxton, meanwhile, is running his own 18-day “Come and Take It” bus tour that began Oct. 17 in Rockwall, USA Today reported.

“Texans are tired of being divided into teams — red versus blue, left versus right, rural versus urban,” Talarico said in the tour announcement quoted by the El Paso Times, adding that he is “traveling across the state to unite working people onto one team.” The tour name borrows the “clear eyes, full hearts, can’t lose” motto of the Texas football classic Friday Night Lights.

Abbott’s planned Laredo appearance adds to a busy calendar for the governor, who is headlining “Let’s Roll” get-out-the-vote events across Texas — including one in San Angelo on Thursday, Oct. 22, per the San Angelo Standard-Times — as he runs for re-election against Democrat Gina Hinojosa. Hinojosa herself rallied supporters in Laredo on Oct. 20, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The convergence on Laredo follows early voting’s opening on Oct. 19. Early voting runs through Oct. 30, and Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3. Webb Watch 956 is covering every campaign’s public statements and stops on the same terms.

Update — October 26, 2026

Talarico's scheduled Laredo stop took place on Sunday, Oct. 25: CBS News Texas reported that Talarico spoke to supporters in Laredo that day as part of his “Clear Eyes, Full Hearts” tour. The same report noted that Republican Ken Paxton rallied supporters in Sanger that day on his “Come and Take It” tour. According to the El Paso Times, Talarico's tour continued to El Paso on Monday, Oct. 26. Webb Watch 956 found no confirmed report of Gov. Greg Abbott's planned Laredo stop as of this update.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, Oct. 21, 2026; El Paso Times, Oct. 16, 2026; San Angelo Standard-Times, Oct. 21, 2026; USA Today, Oct. 19, 2026; CBS News Texas, October 2026; El Paso Times, October 26, 2026.

title: Statewide candidates keep coming to Laredo: Abbott and Talarico plan campaign stops as early voting continues
